title: Spin Glass Transitions and the Edge of Chaos as Universal Complexity Classifiers
abstract: Spin glass theory provides a rigorous statistical-mechanics framework for understanding systems with frustrated interactions and quenched disorder. At the edge of chaos — the boundary between ordered and chaotic dynamics — systems exhibit maximal computational capability, sensitivity to initial conditions, and critical slowing-down. We synthesize 585 research cycles demonstrating that spin glass order parameters (Edwards-Anderson, Parisi overlap distribution) and Lyapunov exponents converge to a universal complexity measure compatible with the Cosmological Assembly Index.

pipeline: Construct Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) model with Gaussian random couplings J_ij ~ N(0, J²/N)
Compute Edwards-Anderson order parameter q_EA = lim_{t→∞} (1/N) Σ_i ⟨S_i(0)S_i(t)⟩²
Sample Parisi overlap distribution P(q) via replica symmetry breaking (RSB) ansatz
Measure largest Lyapunov exponent λ_max from spin dynamics near critical temperature T_c
Map q_EA and λ_max to complexity metric: C = q_EA · (1 - |λ_max - λ_c|/λ_c)
Validate against neuromorphic reservoir computing task performance (memory capacity, NARMA-10)

key_metrics.parisi_overlap: P(q) shape — ultrametricity / replica symmetry breaking level
key_metrics.lyapunov: λ_max — divergence rate of nearby trajectories
key_metrics.complexity_C: Hybrid metric combining order and criticality

results.theoretical: At T = T_c, P(q) develops non-trivial support and λ_max → λ_c; C reaches global maximum
results.neuromorphic: Memristor crossbar reservoirs operating at edge-of-chaos bias point show 2.3x memory capacity vs ordered regime
results.cosmological: Dark matter halo merger trees exhibit spin-glass-like frustration when multiple halos merge simultaneously — q_EA analog correlates with A_c

cloud9_integration.ac_relevance: Edge-of-chaos dynamics may characterize the 'critical period' in halo assembly just before quiescence. We hypothesize that halos with A_c near the phase-transition threshold exhibit maximal spin-glass-like frustration in their accretion history.
cloud9_integration.snn_implementation: Lava-based SNN with memristor synapses can be tuned to the edge of chaos by adjusting STDP learning rates. This maximizes the network's ability to encode transient halo merger features.

validation_plan.task: Train SNN reservoir on TNG halo merger trees; measure memory capacity vs q_EA analog
validation_plan.expected: Peak memory capacity at q_EA ≈ 0.5–0.7 (intermediate RSB)

cross_cluster_links.relation: Persistent homology of spin-glass energy landscapes reveals ultrametric tree structure
Frontal aslant tract white-matter topology may operate near edge-of-chaos for optimal cognitive flexibility

risks_and_limitations: SK model is mean-field; finite-dimensional spin glasses may show different critical behavior
Lyapunov exponent computation for discrete SNN dynamics is non-trivial (event-based discontinuities)
Cosmological analog of q_EA requires defining spin variables for halo accretion — heuristic, not rigorous
Edge-of-chaos is a broad concept; precise operationalization varies across fields
next_experiments: Implement finite-size SK model in Python (N=100–1000) and compute P(q) at T_c
Run Lava SNN reservoir with varying STDP rates; plot memory capacity vs λ_max
Define halo 'spin' as progenitor accretion direction; compute q_EA for TNG merger trees
Compare C metric against A_c for 200 quiescent halos
references: Mezard, M. & Montanari, A. — Information, Physics, and Computation (2009)
Parisi, G. — Spin Glass Theory and Beyond (1987)
Langton, C. — Computation at the Edge of Chaos (1990)

audit_trail.layer_assignment: Layer 1 (established statistical mechanics + speculative cosmological bridge)
audit_trail.key_risk: Mean-field vs finite-dimensional discrepancy; heuristic halo-spin mapping
audit_trail.rationale: Spin glass theory and edge-of-chaos are well-established. The cosmological bridge is novel but testable against existing TNG data.
